newsitem.title: ITALY: Key Italian local elections called for April 27.
newsitem.headline: Key Italian local elections called for April 27.

text.p: Local elections for 1,138 Italian cities and towns, including Milan and Turin, will take place on April 27, the interior ministry said in statement on Monday.
Some nine million people will be eligible to vote in the largest ballot since the Italian general election last April.
Second round run-offs between the top two candidates in places where no one wins more than 50 percent of the vote will be held on May 11.
Italians will also elect five provincial governments for Mantua, Pavia, Gorizia, Ravenna and Viterbo, on April 27.
Around 100 of the towns and cities involved in the forthcoming vote have populations of more than 15,000.
The most closely watched battle will be in Italy's second city, Milan, which is currently controlled by the separatist Northern League party.

The League, whose popularity has waned since last year's general election when it took 10 percent of the national vote, has not yet decided if it will team up with other political forces to fight the local election.
Other cities to hold local elections in April include Novara, Belluno and Pordenone in the north, Siena and Terni in the centre and Catania, Lecco and Agrigento in the South.
A broad coalition of centre-left parties grouped in the Olive Tree alliance, won last April's general election.
Another wave of important local elections, involving Rome, Naples, Venice and Palermo, are due to be held in the autumn.
